title: Given everything, he still wanted more.
subtitle: Greed that forgets the Giver
then: After the wealth, the sons present at his side and the smooth life, {trap}he desires that Allah give him more{/trap}. Ibn Kathir notes this came with ungratefulness for blessings he knew well. He wanted the gifts and rejected the Giver.
now: The phone is two years old and works fine, but the new one dropped. The salary rose, and the target rose with it. {trap}More is never enough when thanks never comes first.{/trap}
old: Once I get a bit more, then I will feel settled and grateful.
new: Gratitude for what I already have is the only way more ever feels like enough.
try: Before asking Allah for anything today, thank Him for three things you already have.

title: No. He stubbornly stood against Our signs.
subtitle: Obstinacy after knowing
then: Ibn Kathir says obstinate here means {trap}ungratefulness for his blessings after knowing them{/trap}. Al-Walid had even admitted the Quran was not poetry or madness. The problem was not that he did not know. {idea}He knew, and refused.{/idea}
now: You know you owe your sister an apology. You know that habit is wrong. {trap}You just dig in, because changing would mean admitting it.{/trap} Stubbornness is harder to fix than ignorance.
old: I am not stubborn, I just have not been convinced yet.
new: Sometimes I am convinced and still refuse, and that refusal is the real barrier.
try: Think of one thing you already know is right but resist. Take one step toward it today.

title: Instead of more, an uphill climb.
subtitle: The reverse of the easy road
then: He wanted more, and was told of Saud. Mujahid said it is {trap}a harsh portion of the torment{/trap}, and Qatadah said a torment with no break for relief. His life had been made smooth. Its end, after denial, was described as a climb.
now: You coast for years because everything is easy: grades, job, friends. {idea}Ease can hide how far you have drifted.{/idea} The climb is easier to start now, on your own feet, than to be forced into later.
old: My life has been easy, so the next one will be too.
new: Ease here is not a promise of ease there; it is a chance to climb toward Him now.
try: Choose one small uphill thing for Allah today, like praying on time when it is inconvenient.

title: He thought it over, and plotted a label.
subtitle: Using a good mind to avoid the truth
then: Ibn Kathir explains he {trap}contemplated what he should say about the Quran{/trap} and deliberated over what statement to invent against it. His tribe had pressured him, saying he only visited Abu Bakr for food. He needed an answer that saved face.
now: Someone you respect corrects you. Instead of asking if they are right, your mind starts drafting the comeback, the spin, the reason they are biased. {trap}Clever thinking, aimed the wrong way.{/trap}
old: I am thinking carefully, so I must be reasoning honestly.
new: Careful thought is only honest when it is looking for the truth, not a way out.
try: Next time you feel defensive today, ask yourself first: what if they are right?

title: Ruin on him, for how he schemed.
subtitle: The scheme itself is condemned
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {trap}a supplication against him{/trap}. It is not the final words alone that are condemned, but {idea}how he deliberated{/idea}, the careful process of building a lie against the Quran.
now: You plan how to word the message so you look innocent. You think through the excuse for the manager before you are late. {idea}The planning is its own deed.{/idea} Allah sees the drafts, not just the final send.
old: As long as I do not say it, my plotting does not count.
new: Scheming against the truth is itself a deed Allah sees and judges.
try: Catch one moment today where you are rehearsing a spin, and choose the plain truth instead.

title: And again, ruin on him for how he schemed.
subtitle: Said twice because it was serious
then: The curse is repeated: {trap}once more, how he plotted{/trap}. The Quraysh had said that if Al-Walid accepted Islam, all of Quraysh would follow. His label of magic was meant to steer everyone. {idea}One man's scheme was shaping a whole people.{/idea}
now: A team leader who dismisses a good idea in front of everyone. A popular friend who mocks something good. {idea}When people follow you, your words weigh more.{/idea} The repeat is a reminder of how serious that is.
old: What I say is just my opinion; it does not affect anyone.
new: If people look to me, my words can lead them toward truth or away from it.
try: Use your voice today to praise one good thing in front of others.

title: Then he looked again.
subtitle: A second look that could have saved him

key.label: What a second look is for

then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}he thought again and deliberated{/idea}. Qatadah reports he admitted the Quran had sweetness and elegance and was not poetry. The second look showed him the truth. {trap}He used it to choose a better label.{/trap}
now: You read the verse twice. You watch the talk again. Something in you softens. {reward}That second look is a door opening.{/reward} What you do in the next minute matters more than how clever your thoughts are.
old: Looking again just helps me build a better case.
new: A second look is a mercy that lets me turn back before I decide.
try: Re-read one verse today that moved you before, and let it move you again.

title: Then he frowned and scowled.
subtitle: The face of a heart refusing
then: Ibn Kathir describes him {trap}contracting his eyebrows together and frowning{/trap}, then scowling in disgust. He had just admitted the Quran's sweetness. The frown was his whole self pushing it away.
now: Someone reminds you to pray while you are mid-game. Your face does it before you say a word. {trap}That flash of irritation is worth noticing.{/trap} It shows what your heart is resisting.
old: My reaction to a reminder is just a mood, it means nothing.
new: The frown I give the truth tells me where my heart is pushing back.
try: Next time a reminder annoys you today, smile instead and say: JazakAllahu khayran.

title: Then he turned his back, too proud to submit.
subtitle: Pride is what walked away
then: Ibn Kathir says he {trap}turned away from the truth and arrogantly refused{/trap} to accept and submit to the Quran. His tribe had mocked him. Being seen to follow the Prophet ﷺ felt like losing his standing.
now: Your teenager is right and you know it, but saying so feels like losing. Your junior at work has the better plan. {trap}Pride turns your back for you.{/trap} {idea}Humility is just turning around.{/idea}
old: Admitting I was wrong will make me look weak.
new: Pride, not proof, is what usually makes me turn my back on the truth.
try: Say I was wrong to someone today about one small thing, plainly.

title: He called it old magic, passed down.
subtitle: A label to stop people listening
then: After all his thinking, he said {trap}this is nothing but magic from of old{/trap}, meaning, Ibn Kathir says, magic Muhammad ﷺ received from those before him. Quraysh had tried poet, soothsayer, madman. They settled on magic.
now: Cult. Old-fashioned. Extremist. Boring. {trap}A quick label lets you stop thinking about something.{/trap} Watch for the moment you file an uncomfortable truth under a word so you can move on.
old: Once I have named what something is, I do not need to think about it.
new: A label can be a way of running from what I do not want to hear.
try: Pick one thing you dismissed with a label, and spend five minutes actually listening to it.

title: This is only a man talking, he said.
subtitle: Shrinking the word of Allah to a human speech
then: Ibn Abbas reports Al-Walid first told Quraysh {idea}his speech is from the Words of Allah{/idea}. Under pressure he ended with {trap}this is nothing but the word of a human being{/trap}. If it is only a man's words, there is nothing to obey.
now: You read a verse and think: that was for them, back then. Or: that is just how scholars read it. {trap}It shrinks the verse until it no longer asks anything of you.{/trap}
old: Some of the Quran is just for its time, so it does not apply to me.
new: It is Allah's word, so it is speaking to me now, not just to them then.
try: Read one verse today and ask: what is this asking of me, this week?

title: I will bring him into Saqar.
subtitle: The end of the road he chose
then: After his label, the answer: Saqar. Ibn Kathir says it means {trap}engulfing him from all sides{/trap}. The verses before it showed every step: he thought, looked, frowned, turned back in pride, and spoke. {idea}The end was built one choice at a time.{/idea}
now: Nobody wakes up far from Allah overnight. It is one skipped prayer, one rationalised habit, one proud no. {idea}Each step is small, which means each step back is small too.{/idea}
old: I am not heading anywhere bad; I have only made a few small choices.
new: Paths are built from small steps, so one small step can also turn me back.
try: Undo one small step away from Allah today: return to one thing you dropped.

title: And what will tell you what Saqar is?
subtitle: A question that makes you stop
then: Ibn Kathir says this question is {idea}to give fright and emphasis to its matter{/idea}. The listeners in Makkah were stopped mid-story and made to think: you do not really know what this is.
now: A doctor pauses before giving you results. A teacher stops the class: listen to this part. {idea}The pause is a kindness.{/idea} It means: do not let this pass like background noise.
old: I have heard about Hell so often that it no longer affects me.
new: The Quran pauses here so I will not treat this as background noise.
try: When you next hear a warning verse, pause recitation for a moment and make dua for safety.

title: It spares nothing and leaves nothing.
subtitle: No half measures in that fire
then: Ibn Abbas reports these verses were revealed about Al-Walid up to this very line. Ibn Kathir says those in it remain {trap}neither living nor dying{/trap}. It was said plainly to a city still able to change its answer.
now: The door of repentance is open today, on an ordinary weekday, while you sit with a coffee. {reward}The fire spares nothing; Allah's mercy right now spares everyone who turns.{/reward}
old: Even if I end up in trouble, it will not be that bad.
new: That fire spares nothing, so I turn to the mercy that is open now.
try: Make sincere istighfar today for one specific sin, naming it to Allah in private.
